sessionTitle: Move from data to intelligence with Oracle MCP and Microsoft IQ

announcements.name: Managed, hosted Oracle MCP servers for Oracle Database@Azure
announcements.shortDescription: Oracle offers native, managed MCP servers in both Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and for databases running at Azure, with the MCP server itself provided at no additional cost (customers pay only for database and AI tooling usage).
announcements.longDescription: Oracle now offers managed, hosted MCP servers natively in both Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and for Oracle Databases running at Azure. Customers or partners can define the characteristics of the MCP server—what tools are made available and how authentication works—and Oracle runs it for them at no additional cost. The only charges are for using the database or the AI tooling; the MCP server itself is free. Setup begins with defining a database connection using a set of credentials (such as a proxy user tied to an identity domain) that shape what data the AI can see.

announcements.name: MCP servers for Oracle AI Database since July
announcements.shortDescription: Oracle has shipped MCP server support for its AI Database, extending now into cloud-hosted managed offerings.
announcements.longDescription: Jeff Smith notes that Model Context Protocol (MCP) emerged in late 2024 and gained rapid adoption throughout 2025. Oracle has had MCP servers for Oracle AI Database since July, and is now extending support to cloud-hosted managed offerings in both Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and for Oracle Databases running at Azure.

announcements.name: End-to-end identity propagation via Entra ID and OAuth 2
announcements.shortDescription: A user's Azure Entra ID identity is propagated into the Oracle database itself through an OBO token flow, so the database applies its own security rules to the agent's queries as if the user connected directly.
announcements.longDescription: After an agent is registered as an MCP client, an OAuth 2 workflow handles authentication: the user logs in, their Azure Entra ID credentials are verified, and they grant the agent permission to act on their behalf via an OBO (on-behalf-of) token, after which the agent obtains an access token without repeated logins. The user's Entra ID identity is then propagated into the Oracle database itself, so the database sees the user as themselves rather than the agent. This allows Oracle's own security rules to be applied to the agent's queries as if the user connected directly, provided the user's group membership grants access to the relevant resources.
